buildings.role: The documentation site behind turborepo.dev: MDX content plus the Next.js app that renders it.
The binary crate: a main() that installs panic handling and hands every command to turborepo-cli, plus the Rust integration tests.
An internal Next.js operator app that creates agent workspaces in Vercel Sandboxes and keeps a record and transcript of each one.
About a hundred complete monorepos, each with a recorded lockfile and a meta.json, that check-lockfiles.ts prunes and re-validates.
Repository detection and package discovery: infers the package manager, reads workspaces and builds the package dependency graph.
Parses npm, pnpm, yarn and bun lockfiles and derives the per-package dependency subgraph used for fine-grained cache invalidation.
Codemod transformations that rewrite turbo.json and package files when a feature is deprecated or the config format changes.
The CLI composition layer: argument parsing, command dispatch, the version shim and the wiring of the run, daemon and query crates.
Terminal output: colours, spinners, per-task prefixes and log writers, plus the interactive TUI mode.
Task output caching: a local filesystem cache and the Vercel remote cache behind a multiplexer and an async worker pool.
The Rust workspace root: members are crates/turborepo*, turbo-trace and the native part of packages/turbo-repository, on edition 2024.
Git integration: changed-file detection, reading previous lockfile versions and hashing files through ls-tree, hash-object and libgit2.
Cross-platform file watching over FSEvents, inotify and ReadDirectoryChanges, turning raw events into derived data such as changed packages.
Parses and validates turbo.json, including comments, and is the source of truth for task definitions and repository settings.
Builds the task dependency graph from turbo.json and the package graph, then orchestrates parallel execution over it.
An in-repo agent skill documenting turbo.json tasks, caching, filtering and boundaries, with a command and reference pages beside it.
Spawns and supervises the child processes that run task commands, with PTY support, signal forwarding and graceful shutdown.
Login against the Vercel API: device authorization grant, token refresh, SSO team verification and token storage.
The per-repository background daemon, a gRPC server that answers file hash queries and reports package changes to warm later runs.
One turbo run: resolves package scope, loads the engine, then executes tasks with the cache, process manager and run summary attached.
The create-turbo scaffolder, which copies one of the examples into a new repository and installs it.
Loads and merges configuration by precedence: turbo.json, then global and local config files, then environment variables, then CLI flags.
Checks that imports between packages respect the tag-based rules configured in turbo.json.
Fixture monorepos, one per behaviour under test, that the Rust integration tests in the turborepo crate run the real binary against.
Resolves which packages a run covers, applying --filter patterns, --affected change detection and glob matching.
HTTP client for the remote cache API: authentication, artifact upload and download, and telemetry endpoints, aimed at Vercel by default.
Runs an individual task: checks the cache, spawns the process, handles its output and saves the result back to the cache.
Computes each task's cache key from file contents, environment variables and task configuration; the hash that decides a cache hit.
The npm package users install: a bin shim plus optional per-platform dependencies that deliver the matching compiled binary.
The repository's own turbo configuration: task pipeline, global pass-through environment variables and the future flags it dogfoods.

ai.summary: Turborepo is a Rust build system for JavaScript monorepos. The tool is a 74-crate workspace: turborepo-cli takes the command line, turborepo-run and turborepo-engine build the task graph, and turborepo-task-executor runs it. Around it sit npm-published JavaScript packages, a documentation site, and four large fixture directories: examples, integration tests, lockfile fixtures and template apps.

strengths: The Rust workspace is cut along real seams: caching, source control, lockfiles, file watching and the daemon are each their own crate.
Correctness is pinned by recorded artefacts rather than prose: lockfile fixtures for every package manager and snapshot tests for the CLI help.
Every published example is a real workspace that CI refreshes on release, so the getting-started path cannot rot silently.
Breaking configuration changes ship with codemods, so upgrading is a command rather than a manual edit.
Only 13 open issues against a repository of this size suggests the tracker is actively groomed.
concerns: Fixtures dominate the tree: examples, lockfile-tests, turborepo-tests and apps together outweigh the source by several times, so the top level hides where the code is.
A single run is spread across turborepo-cli, turborepo-run, turborepo-engine, turborepo-task-hash and turborepo-task-executor, so following one command end to end means crossing five crates.
The repository mixes two toolchains, Rust and pnpm JavaScript, so a contributor needs both set up before anything builds.
